answer: Articulation-point detection resists sybils: the trust graph is scanned for cut vertices whose removal disconnects a region, and influence flowing ONLY through such a bridge is discounted. An umber cluster of fakes hanging off a single articulation point is structurally exposed — cut that one ferrous node and the whole region falls away from the honest component. Honest identities sit in biconnected neighborhoods with no single point of failure; a sybil region dangling past one bridge cannot fake redundant connectivity.
